newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - December 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - December 19.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
FINANCIAL TIMES
-- BA TO SELL ITS 25 PERCENT STAKE IN USAIR

British Airways has said it plans to sell its 24.6 percent stake in USAir, bringing to an end a four-year alliance. The pairing degenerated into acrimony earlier this year when BA announced plans for an alliance with American Airlines, a move which prompted legal action from USAir. Shares in BA rose 9.5p to 601p following news of the sale plans, as analysts saw the decision as an indication of BA's confidence that it will secure regulatory approval for the American alliance.
-- FORMER BA ADVISER WINS 'DIRTY TRICKS' LIBEL CASE

A public relations consultant has been awarded 20,000 stg after winning a libel case over claims made in a book on the dispute between British Airways and Virgin Atlantic. Brian Basham, who formerly worked for British Airways, was described by the book as acting in a disreputable way. The book, called "Dirty Tricks," documents the bitter dispute between the two airlines which resulted in BA making an unprecedented public apology to Virgin.
-- WAY CLEAR FOR GENETIC MAIZE SALES IN EU

The European Commission has approved genetically modified maize, clearing the way for it to be sold without labelling to distinguish it from ordinary maize. The controversial decision has been condemned by environmental and consumer groups, who fear the effects of the grain on cattle and on the food chain. The genetically modified maize has been developed by Swiss chemicals group Ciba Geigy.
-- ENGINEERS REPORT RISE IN EXPORT ORDERS

The latest quarterly survey of business trends from the Engineering Employers' Federation (EEF) has painted a positive picture for the new year, with export orders rising over the past three months despite the strengthening of sterling. The report says the industry is poised to enter the new year on a healthy note, and predicts that overall output will be about 3 percent up in 1996. The EEF also looks forward to companies in the sector increasing employment, after a period of minimal job growth.
-- WOOLWICH AND A&L TO PURSUE CHANGES TO BILL

The Alliance & Leicester and The Woolwich, two of the strongest critics of the government's proposed legislation on building societies, have responded to the final version of the bill by suggesting they may delay their respective planned conversions to bank status. The two building societies are concerned in particular about a clause removing their protection from takeover should they bid for another financial institution.
-- GULF CANADA IN HOSTILE MOVE FOR CLYDE PETROLEUM

International oil and gas group Gulf Canada Resources has launched a 432 million stg hostile bid for UK independent oil company Clyde Petroleum. Acquisition of Clyde would give Gulf access to the UK's North Sea, in addition to production in Australia and Indonesia. The takeover would be Gulf's biggest to date. Shares in Clyde rose 34p to 118.5p on news of the bid, as investors anticipate an increase in the offer.
-- LONDON POWER GROUP AGREES TO 1.3 BILLION STG U.S. BID

London Electricity has become the latest regional electricity company to accept a takeover bid, after it agreed to a 1.3 billion stg offer from US utility Entergy. The deal means that only two of the original 12 electricity companies created by privatisation in 1990 remain independent. Entergy already has investments in South America, Australia and Pakistan, and chairman Ed Lupberger said the London deal was an important step in the company's plans to become a global energy group.
-- U.S. UTILITY MOUNTS $3.5 BILLION CASH AND SHARE BID FOR ADT

U.S. electricity utility Western Resources has launched an unsolicited $3.5 billion bid for home security firm ADT. Western Resources already owns 27 percent of ADT, and completion of the takeover would see it become the biggest security monitoring company in the U.S. and UK. ADT has advised shareholders to take no action until its board has reviewed the offer.
-- NORTHERN'S ADVISERS BUY INTO BID DEFENCE

Broker BZW has bought 1.56 percent of regional electricity company Northern Electric, the client it is advising over its defence against a 782 million stg hostile takeover bid from US utility CalEnergy. Northern's financial adviser, Schroders, bought a 0.74 percent stake in the company. The advisers said the move was an attempt to support Northern's defence against a bid which they claim is far too low.
-- CONSORTIUM PLANS TO DEVELOP ADVANCED CHIPS

A consortium has been formed involving many of the world's leading semiconductor chip makers to develop advanced microprocessor chips. The new generation of chips is expected to be twice as fast as present computer 'brain' chips and to cost half as much. Companies involved in the consortium include Toshiba, NEC, Sony and SGS Thomson.
